# CellML model authoring

For an account-backed workspace, fetch the immutable Physiome exposure artifact with authenticated MCP and preserve its changeset, URL, bytes, license rule, and checksum. For local/offline work, pin those facts beside the local artifact. Use `LibCellMLBioModule` and libCellML parsing/validation/code generation; do not copy equations into handwritten replacements.

Trace CellML components and variables to friendly Biosimulant ports with explicit units. Document initialization, imported components, generated-code/runtime versions, numerical assumptions, and supported interventions in the MTS. Test source validation, unit consistency, mapped inputs/outputs, representative behavior, and reproducibility. Keep physiological interpretation and unsupported clinical claims explicit in caveats.

When opting into model compatibility, add contracts to the existing `io` ports
for source variable identity, physical quantity, units, biological context, and
time semantics. Preserve missing CellML annotations as missing evidence that can
produce `UNKNOWN`; do not invent ontology mappings.

Keep the source-faithful time-course adapter on its supported temporal hook. Any
new finite preprocessor uses `execute(inputs, *, context)` with the imported enum
member `ExecutionPolicy.ONCE_BEFORE_RUN`; never use the invalid quoted uppercase
string `"ONCE_BEFORE_RUN"`.


## Visualization deliverables

Before authoring, call `get_biosimulant_authoring_contract` with topic `visualization`.
The complete catalog contains timeseries, bar, scatter, heatmap, graph, table, image,
structure3d and text, including payload examples, limits and retained artifact rules.
Almost every scientific Lab needs a useful visual of actual computed outputs; choose
the type by the user's question rather than always emitting a table. Record expected
views, source outputs, units and caveats in the MRS; record render/schema, owning module,
typed wiring, lifecycle, artifact retention and executable checks in the MTS.
Implement reusable `BioModule.visualize()` and declare `lab.yaml` visualization requirements
(or a justified opt-out for infrastructure-only work). Inspect actual composed results,
check plotted values against typed outputs, and verify artifacts and reopening. Missing
or invalid required views block qualification/publication. Ad-hoc Studio chat charts
do not satisfy this contract. Historical Labs without a declaration remain compatible.
